<reason>Side B (PRO) wins a close, high-quality debate. A's core route was a forced choice: aggregate-only access can't establish causation, individual histories can't be anonymized. B defused it with a coherent hybrid — pseudonymized histories computed inside a secure room, only noise-checked aggregates leaving — grounded in ordinary real-world practice (census microdata, tax and hospital records). A's rejoinder that such aggregates are "too coarse" for cascade questions is asserted rather than shown, and sits awkwardly beside A's own concession that sworn auditors can safely view the same data, which powers B's "proves too much" symmetry (if the data is safe enough for ad-targeters and confidential auditors, it is safe enough for logged, penalized researchers). B also answered both pressure questions directly and coherently, while B's authoritarian-precedent rebuttal (regimes coerce without waiting for our laws; distributed published science is harder to capture than backroom deals) at least neutralized A's front-door scare. A executed superbly — the layered A4.3 dissolution of the "exposing or whitewashed" trap (users exposed at the data layer, findings curated at the control layer) was the best single rebuttal of the debate, and A's closing was crisp. But A's claim that B "never resolved" that trap only works if one ignores A4.3's own logic being partially answered by B's logging-and-sanctions design, and B's minor mischaracterization in B4.5 ("never resolved") is a small accuracy cost. On the motion as written, CON needed the impossibility claim to survive, and it only half-survives; B's institutional analogies were never squarely disanalogy-ed. Edge to PRO on substance with near-even execution and rhetoric.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A's pressure Q1 forced B to pick between non-causal aggregates and non-anonymous histories; B's A1 answer — pseudonymized individual histories computed inside the secure room with only noise-checked aggregates leaving — was the decisive exchange, converting A's dichotomy into a workable model that A could thereafter only attack by assertion.</best_rebuttal>
